ink-tab.displayName: Ink Mid / Tab (6.29:1; identical hex for two roles on the dark theme only, distinct on light)

ink-ghost.displayName: Ink Ghost (5.98:1, the tightest ramp tier)

ink-on-wash.displayName: Ink On Wash (role tier for text over --bg-hover/--bg-active; printed contrast figures in the source comment did not reproduce under recomputation)

mountain-gray.displayName: Mountain Gray (structure; sole consumer is the hardcoded mix inside --bg-active)

valley-blue.displayName: Valley Blue (attention owed; contract amendment, was named ochre)

graphite-steel.displayName: Graphite Steel (database/MCP; source comment also calls this value "blue-violet", a leftover from a previous world's teal, which was a different hex)

identity-violet.displayName: Identity Violet (one of six accent tokens rotated for project/group identity, not a dedicated identity-only hue)

headline.purpose: The ceiling of the ramp at 15.5px: the bridge-missing fallback lockup and the remove-project dialogue title. 2 declarations.

title.purpose: Brand lockup and view/profile headers. 6 declarations.

body.purpose: Prose and stream text; also the base size on html. 24 declarations.

label.purpose: Section headings. Only the sidebar's own PROJECTS heading carries the intended 0.08em tracking; a full scan found 12 distinct hardcoded letter-spacing values (0.02em-0.18em) across 14 files, with Sidebar.vue alone using three different values on three elements. 53 declarations at this size overall.

meta.purpose: The most-used size in the application, 66 declarations. Secondary lines, timestamps, pills, footer readings.

caption.purpose: Sub-labels, chip text, agent lines. 50 declarations.

micro.purpose: The floor of the ramp. 25 declarations.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono, 11.5px, weight 600 on the button/pill/chip/badge idiom. The .mono CSS class itself resolves to the sans face, not this font; see The Earned Monospace Rule.

glyph.purpose: Icon and symbol glyphs are sized to optical weight, outside the ramp by design. Four selectors are the design-detector hook's current documented carve-out: .group-caret (8px), .rd-icon (17px), .empty-icon (22px), .ni-icon (20px). A fifth, McpView.vue's .empty-ico (26px), is the same kind of glyph but is not yet in that carve-out.

shadows.name: elev
shadows.purpose: Default for any card or dialogue. A lip of light on an edge, not elevation.

shadows.name: green-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary (foil-gold) buttons only. The one place the system permits a coloured shadow.

shadows.name: shadow-dlg
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogues only, the sole tier allowed a real cast shadow.

motion.name: sbFade
motion.purpose: Small unrelated status squares/dots (parallel-agent indicators, the update-banner dot). Not the sidebar's signature idiom, which carries no motion of its own.

motion.name: sbIn
motion.purpose: Entrance for dialogues, context menus, the armed button state.

motion.name: sbPulse
motion.purpose: Expanding-ring pulse on InboxView's own group-dot.

motion.name: sbBlink
motion.purpose: Terminal caret. Steps rather than eases, because a caret does not fade.

motion.name: inboxPeekGlow
motion.purpose: Collapsed-inbox reopen badge, while items are pending.

motion.name: gs-spin
motion.purpose: The global loading spinner ring, the one element deliberately exempt from the flat-corner rule because it rotates.

motion.name: now-line (REMOVED)
motion.purpose: The previous world's one shared, authored motion (a breathing rule crossing every lane) was deleted outright with the score it belonged to. Nothing replaced it; a sheet at rest does not pulse.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action colour, filled foil gold under a shallow raking highlight.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(118deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.18) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 46%), linear-gradient(135deg, #D4AF37, #B8952A); color: #17181B; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 14px; border: none; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; box-shadow: 0 6px 18px -6px rgba(212,175,55,0.45); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #E2C25C; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #D4AF37; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }

components.name: Armed Button
components.description: Second step of a destructive confirmation, filled valley blue. Enters with a rise-and-fade so the state change is visible.
components.css: .ds-btn-armed { background: #8CB8E4; color: #17181B; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 14px; border: none; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; animation: dsIn 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-armed:hover { background: #A6C9EC; } .ds-btn-armed:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #D4AF37; outline-offset: 2px; } @keyframes dsIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(5px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The cancel-and-destroy idiom: transparent at rest, hover turns red-pencil rather than the neutral foil-gold that Quiet uses.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #9B9A94; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(244,244,242,0.22); border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: rgba(232,112,92,0.5); color: #E8705C; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #D4AF37; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Code-plate fill with a hairline border. The 1px foil-gold focus outline is the only focus treatment in the system.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #141518; color: #E6E5E1; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid rgba(244,244,242,0.22); border-radius: 0; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #A3A29C; } .ds-input:focus { outline: 1px solid #D4AF37; }

components.name: Risk Chip (High)
components.description: The loudest of three risk steps: low is a bare border, medium adds valley blue, high adds a red-pencil wash behind the border.
components.css: .ds-chip-risk-high { display: inline-block; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10px; color: #E8705C; background: rgba(232,112,92,0.07); border: 1px solid rgba(232,112,92,0.45); border-radius: 0; padding: 1px 6px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Count Badge
components.description: Counts decisions a human owes. Sharp-cornered like everything else in this world, not the round pill a badge name might suggest; the value-reporting idiom used to mean fully round and now means fully square.
components.css: .ds-badge-count { display: inline-block; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10.5px; color: #8CB8E4; background: rgba(140,184,228,0.13); border: 1px solid rgba(140,184,228,0.35); border-radius: 0; padding: 0 6px; line-height: 16px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.description: Settings toggle. Sharp-cornered rectangle, not a pill; fills foil gold when on.
components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; width: 38px; min-width: 38px; height: 21px; border: none; border-radius: 0; background: rgba(244,244,242,0.22); cursor: pointer; } .ds-switch--on { background: #D4AF37; } .ds-switch__knob { position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 17px; height: 17px; border-radius: 0; background: #A3A29C; transition: all 0.15s ease; } .ds-switch--on .ds-switch__knob { left: auto; right: 2px; background: #17181B; } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #D4AF37; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Mark (Held)
components.description: Signature component. A held lane draws one crease scored but not yet folded, valley blue, with no motion of its own. Paired with the plain word "Needs you" via markTitle() so the shape never has to be learned on its own.
components.css: .ds-mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; color: #A3A29C; } .ds-mark--held { color: #8CB8E4; }

components.name: Status Mark (Deploying)
components.description: A working lane draws three facets opening out of the packet, foil gold, the same hue as the primary action because working is the action state in this system.

components.name: Project Lane
components.description: The application's real navigation: a per-lane 1px fold tick in the project's rotated identity colour, and a mountain-gray wash on the selected lane. Carries no staff, no now-line, and no per-lane animation.
components.html: api-server
components.css: .ds-lane { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; padding: 8px 18px 8px 13px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease; } .ds-lane:hover { background: rgba(244,244,242,0.06); } .ds-lane:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #D4AF37; } .ds-lane--active { background: color-mix(in srgb, #B9B6AE 12%, transparent); border-radius: 8px; } .ds-lane__tick { position: absolute; left: 1px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); opacity: 0.75; color: #A99BD0; } .ds-lane--active .ds-lane__tick { opacity: 1; } .ds-lane__name { flex: 1; min-width: 0; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: #D2D1CC; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-lane--active .ds-lane__name { color: #F4F4F2; }

narrative.overview:
The thesis is a sheet, scored and folded flat, deployed by one pull. It is a deliberate double refusal: not the dark-IDE-plus-neon default, not the white SaaS dashboard, and not this project's own previous world either, which drew every state as music notation and asked the developer to learn that vocabulary first. This world asks the developer to learn nothing.

The material is the same physical object in two lights, not two designs. In carbon fibre (#17181B), the ground reads as dense composite under a faint sixty-degree crease lattice; on paper (#F7F7F7), the same lattice scores darker, because ink marking paper is subtractive while a crease catching light on carbon is additive. Three semantic accents carry meaning and meaning alone: foil gold is the one action colour, valley blue is attention owed, the red-pencil mark is a correction. A finished lane earns no hue at all, drawing a locked fold instead of a coloured badge. Project identity is a separate concern from state, carried by a 1px fold tick colour-rotated from the same six accent tokens the rest of the system uses for meaning.

This build's own finish clause states that unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished. Several of the direction contract's own promises (angled hairlines, mono spec labels on identifiers, the flat-round exception being singular rather than threefold) are not yet built; this document records those gaps as open rather than smoothing them into the description.
keyCharacteristics: Two token sets, one object: html.sb-light and :root are the same sheet under carbon-fibre and paper light, sharing all 17 files that consume the semantic accent tokens by name.
Three accents carry state (foil gold for action/working, valley blue for attention owed, red-pencil for error); a finished lane carries none.
Corners are cut, not rounded: --rc and --rp are both 0px, with three named, deliberate circle exceptions (a spinner, a connection dot, a tally dot).
Project identity is a 1px fold tick in the lane's own colour, rotated across the same six accent tokens used for state elsewhere, never a coloured edge bar.
Every translucent accent wash is derived from its solid token with color-mix(), never a hardcoded accent rgba() triplet.
Essentially no authored motion. The previous world's one signature animation, a shared now-line breath, was deleted outright and nothing replaced it.

rules.name: The Two-Track Wash Rule
rules.body: Every translucent wash and accent border derives from its solid token by construction, color-mix(in srgb, var(--token) N%, transparent), never a hardcoded accent rgba() hue. Verified at 128 declarations across 14 files, with zero stray accent rgba() triplets found anywhere in the renderer.

rules.name: The Contract Amendment Rule
rules.body: When a named material colour cannot clear the contrast floor without colliding with another state signal, the amendment is recorded in the token's own code comment rather than silently changed. Valley blue's substitution for the contract's original ochre attention-owed colour is the current example.

rules.name: The Fine Gets No Hue Rule
rules.body: A finished lane draws a locked fold in neutral ink, not a success colour. Only three states carry colour (held, working, error); finished/ended is deliberately colourless so it never competes with a lane that still needs the developer.

rules.name: The Earned Monospace Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for content that is genuinely code, a command, a path, or terminal output, plus the button/pill/chip idiom that borrows its voice. The .mono CSS class resolves to the sans face; reaching for it expecting monospace is the mistake this rule exists to name.

rules.name: The Available But Unadopted Rule
rules.body: The direction contract states, present tense, that identifiers carry mono spec labels via a --track-label token and a .spec-label utility, and that hairlines terminate at an angle via a .scored-rule utility. Both utilities are real, working CSS; both are applied nowhere, zero call sites across every .vue file and the production build. The label-tracking drift .spec-label was meant to close (12 distinct hardcoded values, 0.02em-0.18em, across 14 files) is unchanged from before the utility existed. The parallelogram shear and corner tabs from the source world's component board go a step further: they are not even declared, absent rather than unadopted.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the overlay/dialogue tier casts a real shadow. A card that wants to lift off its panel is asking for the wrong tier.

dos: Do call the attention-owed colour Valley Blue, and the error colour Red-Pencil, not "ochre" or "red" loosely; the contract amendment recorded in the code exists precisely because those two nearly collided.
Do treat --rc and --rp as 0px for everything except the three named round point-markers (.gs-ring, .mcp-dot, .foot-dot) and the small 2px/6px/8px interactive-patch exceptions.
Do derive every wash from its solid token with color-mix(in srgb, var(--token) N%, transparent). Never hardcode an accent rgba() triplet.
Do keep JetBrains Mono for terminal output, commands, and the button/pill/chip/badge idiom. Everything else is the system sans stack; there is no serif face anywhere in this world.
Do add explicit dark and light values for any new token; --bg-active is currently the one known exception and should be treated as a gap, not a pattern.
Do pair any new status mark with a plain-language title or label, the way markTitle() does, so a shape never has to be learned before it is understood.
donts: Don't reintroduce a coloured edge bar for project identity. A fold tick is a 1px stroke; anything thicker is the habit this world refused.
Don't reintroduce backdrop-filter blur on a panel or sticky heading. It appears exactly once in the renderer, on the modal scrim.
Don't add a media query or a percentage-based breakpoint. The target is one fixed desktop window (min-width: 1080px on .panes, matched in BrowserWindow).

Don't assume .spec-label, .scored-rule, or the .chamfer utility are live just because they are declared in styles.css. None is applied anywhere in the current templates or build output; treat each as available but unadopted. The parallelogram shear and corner tabs from the source world's component board are absent entirely, not even declared.
Don't copy the specific decimal contrast figures printed in the --text-on-wash code comments without re-checking them; independent recomputation gives different, though still passing, numbers.

Don't give a new empty-state glyph the class name .empty-title without checking McpView.vue (14.5px/600) and InboxView.vue (13px/400) first; both currently use that exact class name for visually different treatments.
